action_criteria.rationale: A gradual four-year memory decline needs a documented deficit and its cueing profile before any attribution to the vascular burden.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Scheltens MTA grade 3 bilaterally with temporoparietal cortical atrophy, together with Fazekas 2 white matter hyperintensity, two lacunes and one deep microbleed; no cortical or territorial infarct
action_criteria.label: Obtain brain MRI reported in STRIVE-2 terms (FLAIR with a Fazekas grade, T1/T2 for lacunes, DWI for chronicity, SWI for microbleeds and siderosis) together with the medial temporal atrophy grade
action_criteria.rationale: MRI is where both the atrophy grade and the small-vessel burden of this patient with hypertension and atrial fibrillation are measured.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response, rate 74, normal QRS and QTc
action_criteria.label: Record a 12-lead ECG as the baseline for rate and conduction before a cholinesterase inhibitor is started
action_criteria.rationale: She takes bisoprolol for atrial fibrillation; a baseline ECG is reasonable before a drug that slows the heart.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Amyloid positive: CSF Abeta42/40 ratio 0.042 with phospho-tau181 96 pg/mL, or a positive amyloid PET (Centiloid 74)
action_criteria.label: Establish amyloid status with CSF Alzheimer biomarkers or amyloid PET: the question is whether Alzheimer pathology coexists with the vascular burden
action_criteria.rationale: An amnestic syndrome with MTA grade 3 beside a moderate small-vessel burden is the mixed question one amyloid biomarker answers; a lumbar puncture needs apixaban withheld first, which amyloid PET avoids.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Bilateral temporoparietal and posterior cingulate hypometabolism with additional patchy frontal defects adjacent to the white matter lesions
action_criteria.label: Obtain FDG-PET to separate a temporoparietal Alzheimer pattern from the patchy multifocal hypometabolism that follows white matter lesions
action_criteria.rationale: FDG-PET is defensible but adds little once an amyloid biomarker is available.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Cholinesterase inhibitor plus bisoprolol in atrial fibrillation: additive bradycardia, so heart rate and ECG are checked before and after starting
action_criteria.label: Check the cholinesterase inhibitor to be started against her rate-control beta-blocker and the rest of her medication list
action_criteria.rationale: She will be offered a cholinesterase inhibitor for the Alzheimer component while taking bisoprolol for atrial fibrillation, a combination that can cause symptomatic bradycardia.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not diagnose Alzheimer disease alone or vascular dementia alone when both are demonstrated.
Do not stop or reduce apixaban because of a single deep microbleed or her age [ESC_AF_2024].
Do not add an antiplatelet to apixaban for the covert lacunes [ESO_2021_SVD].
Do not omit vascular risk-factor treatment because the memory profile is typical of Alzheimer disease.
Do not prescribe drugs with anticholinergic burden alongside a cholinesterase inhibitor.
Do not attribute the decline to age or to thyroid disease on stable replacement.
required_recommendations: Name the diagnosis as mixed dementia: Alzheimer disease (storage-type amnesia, MTA grade 3, positive amyloid biomarker) with a small-vessel vascular contribution (Fazekas 2, two lacunes) [VASCOG_2014].

Offer a cholinesterase inhibitor for the Alzheimer component (e.g. donepezil 5 mg at night, increased to 10 mg after 4-6 weeks if tolerated), checking heart rate and ECG before and after starting because she takes bisoprolol for atrial fibrillation [NICE_NG97].
Continue apixaban 5 mg twice daily (CHA2DS2-VA 3; no dose-reduction criteria met): a single deep microbleed without falls does not outweigh the stroke-prevention benefit [ESC_AF_2024].
Lower blood pressure gradually to below 130/80 mmHg (148/80 on ramipril 5 mg), checking orthostatic blood pressure at each change [ESO_2021_SVD].

Provide caregiver support and safety planning: supervised medication (her husband already manages it), no return to driving, advance care planning, and review of cognition and function in 6-12 months [NICE_NG97].

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role here: the course is gradual over four years, with no fluctuation, episodes or rapid progression.
No spontaneous parkinsonism, fluctuating alertness, hallucinations or dream enactment: a dopamine transporter scan answers no question in this patient.
No core feature of Lewy body disease; cardiac sympathetic imaging answers no question in this patient.
A gradual four-year amnestic decline is not the subacute multidomain syndrome that indicates paraneoplastic or autoimmune encephalitis antibodies.
MRI is available and not contraindicated; CT cannot show microbleeds, siderosis or small lacunes.
No cortical or territorial infarct and the atrial fibrillation is already anticoagulated: an echocardiogram would not change the diagnosis or the antithrombotic plan.
Atrial fibrillation is already documented and anticoagulated; prolonged rhythm monitoring changes neither the diagnosis nor the treatment.

accepted: Mixed Alzheimer and vascular dementia — biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer pathology with moderate cerebral small-vessel disease

differential.key_features: Storage-type amnesia, MTA grade 3 and a positive amyloid biomarker establish Alzheimer pathology, but Fazekas 2 white matter disease with two lacunes is a second contributor with its own treatment; Alzheimer disease alone would leave it untreated
Storage-type amnesia not rescued by cueing, MTA grade 3 and a positive amyloid biomarker; a Fazekas 2 burden with two lacunes cannot account for this profile
Four years of anticoagulated atrial fibrillation but no cortical or territorial infarct on MRI; the vascular lesions are small-vessel
No fluctuation, hallucinations, spontaneous parkinsonism or dream enactment

key_clinical_evidence: Mixed Alzheimer and vascular pathology is the commonest substrate of dementia at this age and is a diagnosis in its own right
Storage-type amnesia not rescued by cueing with MTA grade 3 is the Alzheimer signature; a Fazekas 2 burden with two lacunes does not produce it
An amyloid biomarker is worth obtaining when a vascular burden coexists with an amnestic syndrome, because it decides whether a cholinesterase inhibitor is indicated
No cortical or territorial infarct after four years of atrial fibrillation: the vascular lesions are small-vessel, and a single deep microbleed does not overturn the anticoagulation indication
A cholinesterase inhibitor with bisoprolol in atrial fibrillation needs heart-rate and ECG monitoring

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: There is no cortical or territorial infarct on MRI after four years of anticoagulated atrial fibrillation; the vascular contribution to this dementia is small-vessel
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a cardioembolic multi-infarct mechanism and directs the workup to an embolic source

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: One microbleed in a deep hypertensive distribution, with no lobar microbleeds, no siderosis and no falls, does not outweigh the stroke-prevention benefit of anticoagulation
red_herrings.intended_effect: Prompts withdrawal of anticoagulation in a patient with atrial fibrillation

sequence_constraints.reason: Document the cognitive deficit before attributing it: imaging read without a cognitive profile invites over-attribution of incidental white matter change
Exclude mass effect and lobar haemorrhage on MRI before a lumbar puncture, and read the vascular and atrophy burden before deciding that an amyloid biomarker is needed

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Giovanna Rizzi is a 78-year-old retired midwife who attends with her husband. He describes four years of gradually worsening memory: she began by forgetting conversations and appointments, then started to lose objects and to repeat questions within minutes, and in the past year has become unable to cook meals she had made for fifty years or to manage her own medication. He is clear that the decline has been gradual throughout, with no abrupt steps he can date, and that memory has been the leading problem from the start rather than slowness or disorganisation. She stopped driving a year ago after two minor collisions in car parks. Her mother and two maternal aunts developed dementia in their seventies. She has had atrial fibrillation for four years, is anticoagulated, and has never had a clinical stroke. She has no hallucinations, no fluctuation in alertness, no dream enactment and no parkinsonian features. Her blood pressure has been in the 140-150 range and her thyroid replacement is stable.

neurological_exam.additional: Pulse irregularly irregular at 74. No frontal release signs. No parkinsonian features.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and cooperative; oriented to person and place, year correct, date incorrect. Repeats the same question three times during the consultation; conversation otherwise coherent, with occasional word-finding pauses. Formal cognitive screening reported separately.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk and tone. Strength 5/5 throughout. No drift.
